title: Before I formed thee (Jeremiah 1)
hook: a young man says I am a child, and God says I knew thee before

segments.voice: Yesterday, the suffering servant, the man of sorrows whose wounds heal others. Your line was by his bruises. Whose burden did you lighten? Day four hundred twenty-one, and a new week, and a new prophet.

He comes from a family of priests in a little village called Anathoth, a few miles north of Jerusalem. The book tells us when: the thirteenth year of King Josiah, about 627 BC, forty years before the city falls. He's young. How young, we don't know; the text only lets him call himself a boy. And he's about to be handed the hardest job in the Bible: to tell his own people, for four decades, that disaster is coming, and to watch them ignore him, and then to watch it happen. His name is Jeremiah, Jeremias in the Douay-Rheims. And it begins with God telling him something about before he was born.
screen: `A PRIEST'S SON FROM ANATHOTH.` → `ABOUT 627 BC.` → `THE HARDEST JOB IN THE BIBLE.`

segments.voice: The word of the Lord comes to him, and in the King James it says: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations." Notice the order. Known first. Then set apart. Then given a job. Before Jeremiah did anything, before he was anything, he was known. And Jeremiah's answer is the most honest thing a person can say to a calling. In the Douay: "Ah, ah, ah, Lord God: behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child." Ah, ah, ah. Stammering. God doesn't argue about his age. He says: say not, I am a child. You'll go where I send you. Be not afraid, for I am with thee. Then God touches his mouth, the way the coal touched Isaiah's lips: I have put my words in thy mouth. Then a strange little test. What do you see, Jeremiah? A branch of an almond tree. Good, God says, for I am watching over my word. In Hebrew it's a pun: almond is shaqed, watching is shoqed. The almond is the first tree to wake up in spring, the watchful tree. The Douay, following the Latin, simply calls it a rod watching. The Catholic Church has taken that first line further than Jeremiah's own story. The Catechism quotes it in its teaching that human life is to be respected and protected from the moment of conception. For Jeremiah, that knowing was what let a stammering boy stand up for forty years.
screen: `KNOWN, SET APART, SENT.` · `AH, AH, AH: I AM A CHILD.` · `I HAVE PUT MY WORDS IN THY MOUTH.` · `ALMOND, THE WATCHFUL TREE.` · then, large: `BEFORE I FORMED THEE IN THE BELLY I KNEW THEE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember you were known first. Settle, and breathe. Notice the things you usually use to explain who you are: your job, your mistakes, your age, what people think of you. Set them down one at a time. Underneath all of them is a fact the prophet heard: before any of that, you were known. If you pray, you can rest in Jeremiah's line: before I formed thee, I knew thee. If you don't, simply let yourself be, for two minutes, without needing to earn it. The bell holds the time.
Before I formed thee. God's first word to Jeremiah: known before he was born, set apart, and sent, even while he said I am a child. Today's word.
Your line: known before the womb. Today, when you feel too young, too old or too small for something, say it once: known first. Day four hundred twenty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Jeremiah's call at Mass, and the Catechism cites Jeremiah 1:5 in its teaching on the dignity of human life from conception.

fork.setup: you're Jeremiah. God has just told you you're a prophet to the nations. you're young and you can't find the words. what do you say?
options: ah, ah, ah, Lord God: I cannot speak, for I am a child.
fork.reveal: Jeremiah stammers that he's only a child. God says: say not, I am a child. be not afraid, for I am with thee.

original.note: Hebrew: almond. It sounds like shoqed, watching: God watches over his word.

trapdoor: what you thought: a lovely verse for baby announcements.
what it means: a frightened young man is told he was known before birth, set apart and sent, and that God will be with him through forty hard years.
what a scholar hears: shaqed, almond, and shoqed, watching, a pun the Latin couldn't keep; and the Catechism cites 1:5 in teaching on the dignity of life.

notes: The title follows the KJV wording ('Before I formed thee'), so 1:5 is quoted from the KJV; the Douay reads 'Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee'. Confirm, or swap to the Douay.
Thirteenth year of Josiah (1:2) as about 627/626 BC; confirm 'about 627'.

CCC 2270 quotes Jeremiah 1:5 on respect for human life from conception; confirm. Reviewer removed a sentence that put words in the Catechism's mouth ('every person is known by God before anyone else sees them'); the script now says only what 2270 teaches.
Shaqed / shoqed wordplay (1:11–12): standard; confirm pointing. The almond as the first tree to blossom in the land is a common gloss.
Jeremiah's ministry of about forty years (627 to after 587 BC): confirm 'four decades'.
